content.title: Gennaro Gattuso apologises after Italy miss out on 2026 World Cup
content.text: Italy head coach Gennaro Gattuso has apologised after his side failed to qualify for the 2026 World Cup.Italy were beaten on penalties by Bosnia and Herzegovina in the qualification playoff final on Tuesday as they missed out on a place at the World Cup for a third successive tournament.Gattuso, 48, would not be drawn on his future in the immediate aftermath of the loss.“The lads didn’t deserve to take a beating like that,” the Italy head coach told Italian broadcaster RAI. “We struggled, we had chances to score, but that’s football. I’m proud of my lads.“We needed this (World Cup qualification) – for ourselves, for Italy, for our sport. A blow like this is hard to take.“I’ve been in football for a few years now; sometimes I’ve celebrated, sometimes I’ve taken blows like today’s.“Personally, I apologise for not making it to the World Cup, but the lads have impressed me.“My future? It’s not important right now. We’ll take this performance, but it hurts, it’s a shame.”Italy had failed to qualify automatically for this summer’s tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada after finishing second to Norway in their qualification group, making them the first former champions to miss three World Cups in a row.Gattuso’s side progressed past Northern Ireland in their playoff semi-final on Thursday, and had led on the night against Bosnia and Herzegovina through Moise Kean’s first-half goal.However, they were reduced to 10 players when Alessandro Bastoni was shown a straight red card for a challenge on Amar Memic, before Haris Tabakovic levelled for Bosnia and Herzegovina in the 79th minute.The game finished 1-1 after extra time and Bosnia and Herzegovina won 4-1 on penalties.Italy have won the World Cup on four occasions, most recently in 2006, a squad which Gattuso was part of. However, they have not progressed past the group stage since their 2006 triumph and have not qualified for the tournament since 2014. Apr 15, 2026Connections: Sports EditionSpot the pattern.
